name: manual_f8a62f
claim: A clean privacy scan is a floor, not proof: a hashed blocklist cannot see facts it has no entry for, and short numbers evade it. Scan every commit being published including other agents' commits on that branch, scan a clean export of tracked files rather than the working tree, and also read the diff as a human would.

decisions.notes: agent-envelope: envelope_id=5463fab0-e48b-41e7-b6e4-3049e22dd814 kind=authorship agent=claude-main actor=claude-main identity_verified=false model=claude-opus-5-5 date=2026-10-31 session_id=session_01ThHx9YdUfr5mQntywvAJ7Z run_id=site-saga-2026-10-31 privacy_tier=redacted | The scanner caught a place name in another agent's commits, but a real count in the same file stayed clean through every scan and was noticed only on reading the source. A local build cache also produced a false finding until the scan ran on a clean export. Zip files must sit inside a scanned folder, since passing a bare file scanned zero files. A generic rule for literal counts was then added to the scanner and proven against the real line; its first version missed that line, so a new rule must be tested on the case that motivated it. | public-handoff=EEG-Action-Center@1f7efa6:docs/headset-log-v2/PEER-HANDOFF.md
